sql:
SELECT fish_date_doy, cls, COUNT(*) as trips, ROUND(SUM(yt), 0) as total_yt, ROUND(AVG(yt / anglers), 3) as avg_yt_per_angler
FROM trips WHERE fish_date_doy >= 190 GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls ORDER BY fish_date_doy DESC, cls;
SELECT ts_doy, ROUND(AVG(wtmp_c), 2) as avg_temp_c FROM pier WHERE ts_doy >= 190 GROUP BY ts_doy ORDER BY ts_doy DESC LIMIT 30;

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

trips = tables['trips']

# Current window: September data (doy 150-220)
sept = trips[(trips['fish_date_doy'] >= 150) & (trips['fish_date_doy'] <= 220)]

# Aggregate by class and week
sept_by_class = sept.groupby('cls').agg({
    'yt': ['sum', 'mean'],
    'anglers': 'mean',
}).round(3)

# By day_range
sept['week'] = (sept['fish_date_doy'] - 150) // 14
sept_by_week = sept.groupby(['week', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': ['sum', lambda x: (x / sept.loc[x.index, 'anglers']).mean()],
    'anglers': 'mean'
}).round(3)

print("September (doy 150-220) by class:")
print(sept_by_class)
print("\n\nRecent weeks by class:")
print(sept_by_week)

# Water temp trend
pier = tables['pier']
pier_sept = pier[(pier['ts_doy'] >= 150) & (pier['ts_doy'] <= 220)]
pier_summary = pier_sept.groupby('ts_doy')['wtmp_c'].mean().round(2)
print("\n\nPier water temp by doy (latest 5):")
print(pier_summary.tail(10))
